directions.title: Does a correctly scheduled noise model close the Stage 1 gap?
directions.odds_event: The re-simulated Stage 1 circuit, scheduled ALAP with FakeFez durations and the job-time calibration, gives P(yes) ≥ 0.40. Control: the same model unscheduled must reproduce 0.25 ± 0.03, or the test is untestable.
directions.question: Once our simulator is set up correctly, does its prediction come close to what the chip actually did in program 1?
known: Program 1's circuit: the chip said yes 50% of the time, the simulator 25%, an ideal device 29%.
Our simulator let waiting qubits decay only if the circuit was timed step by step first; ours was not.
directions.cheapest_test: On a laptop, rebuild program 1's archived circuit, time every step as the chip would, load the chip's error rates from that day, and simulate it again; no chip time.
directions.human_prompt: Is re-running program 1's simulation on the laptop, with a setting fixed that we had left off, to see whether the 0.25-versus-0.50 surprise was our own set-up mistake, worth an afternoon of laptop time (free)? Will it come back a hit?
engine_only: the exact threshold in the pass rule
the paraphrased and negated re-elicitations of the engine's odds
directions.rules_out: Rules out our simulator's missing idle decay as the cause of the 3 November gap: scheduling the circuit correctly moved the prediction by about 0.000 (0.268 against 0.267).
directions.prior_work_line: Vezvaee et al. 2025 (arXiv:2510.18847, Heron r2) found calibration-derived noise models must be scaled 2.3 to 4.0 times to match deep circuits, and Bautra et al. 2026 (arXiv:2603.14607, Eagle) found from_backend twins matched hardware at 95% in only 7 of 96 cases. So a correctly scheduled calibration model is predicted to stay far below the chip's 0.50: fail. Settled bet ng-p3-1: 0.268, fail.

directions.title: Coherent or stochastic? Twirling and DD on the Stage 1 circuit
directions.odds_event: Arm (b), gate and measurement twirling, moves P(yes) toward the corrected-simulator prediction by ≥ 0.125 relative to arm (a), as run, at ≥ 3σ.
directions.question: If we randomly scramble the chip's errors, does program 1's result move clearly toward what the corrected simulator predicts?
known: Program 1 ran with no error scrambling and no idle-qubit protection: IBM's default turns both off.
IBM's published error rates are averages taken with scrambling on, which hides systematic error.
directions.cheapest_test: Re-run program 1's exact circuit on its original qubits in four interleaved versions (as run, random error scrambling, idle-qubit protection pulses, both), 2,000 shots each, plus readout checks.
directions.human_prompt: Is re-running program 1's circuit with its errors deliberately scrambled, to see whether that pulls the chip back toward its simulator, worth about 6 seconds of chip time? Will it come back a hit?
engine_only: the exact threshold in the pass rule
whether the chip agrees with the corrected simulator's prediction
directions.rules_out: Rules out nothing about twirling: the 3 November gap was absent on 4 November (0.246 against 0.269), so there was nothing to close; it set the defaults (twirl off, DD off).
directions.prior_work_line: Cenedese et al. 2023 (arXiv:2211.16114, ibm_lagos) found random echoes made a coherently rotated tomography ellipsoid match the calibration simulator, so twirling is predicted to move a coherent gap toward the simulator; Vezvaee et al. 2025 (arXiv:2510.18847, Heron r2) found a 2.3 to 2.5 times residual even with DD, predicting a stochastic remainder. No twirl on/off versus from_backend exists for deep Heron r2 circuits. Settled ng-p3-2: untestable, no gap that day.

directions.title: Coherent or incoherent, from the archived tomography
directions.odds_event: Family (i), local unitaries plus a ZZ phase, beats family (ii), local Pauli channels plus global depolarising, by ΔlogL ≥ 10 on at least 2 of the 3 archived items.
directions.question: In program 1's saved chip data, are the errors clearly better explained as steady systematic twists than as random noise?
known: Program 1 measured three entangled pairs in detail (9 settings, 4,000 shots each); only one table was made.
IBM's reported error rates are averages that hide systematic error by design (McKay et al. 2023).
directions.cheapest_test: Fit program 1's saved measurements two ways, as steady systematic twists or as random noise, each with seven adjustable numbers, and see which fits clearly better; no chip time.
directions.human_prompt: Is re-analysing program 1's saved entanglement data, to see whether the chip's errors are steady systematic twists rather than random blur, worth an afternoon of laptop time (free)? Will it come back a hit?

directions.rules_out: Rules out, on program 1's three archived pairs, a pure steady-twist account winning a 7-against-7 fit; the contest was decided by the reference state's purity, so P3-5c re-asked it (pass).
directions.prior_work_line: Cenedese et al. 2023 (arXiv:2211.16114, ibm_lagos) and Vezvaee et al. 2025 (arXiv:2510.18847, Heron r2: coherent CZ oscillations plus non-Markovian dephasing) predict coherent and incoherent error together, and McKay et al. 2023 (arXiv:2311.05933) say reported rates hide coherent error. directions.title: Two-friend genuine local friendliness with external settings
directions.odds_event: S > 0 by ≥ 5σ at some n ≥ 1, on the single pre-registered facet (Bong facet 1) and labelling. In the same run, the decohered-friend control is consistent with S ≤ 0 and the no-signalling audit shows no deviation above 3σ.
directions.question: With a few qubits playing 'friends' who observe, does the chip break a limit that must hold if every observation is an absolute fact?
known: Only weaker versions, which reduce to ordinary Bell tests, have been run on quantum chips.
The strong version has been run only with photons, and it needs very clean states (purity at least 0.921).
directions.cheapest_test: Entangle two qubits, give each side a 'friend' of 0 to 4 qubits, fix settings from a public random beacon, and run 9 setting pairs, 2,500 shots each, plus controls.

Laux and Cavalcanti 2026 (arXiv:2609.12527, ibm_marrakesh Heron r2) reached CHSH-type S_LF 0.31-0.47 of 0.83, about 0.87 visibility at 3 CZ, which predicts S of roughly 0.2-0.4 at n=1: positive, near the 5σ bar. directions.title: Is there a one-friend genuine LF inequality?
directions.odds_event: A non-Bell local-friendliness facet exists in the one-friend 3×2 or 3×3 scenario that quantum theory violates with a white-noise tolerance of at least 15% (mathematics-graded).
directions.question: With one observing 'friend' and three settings, is there a test stronger than an ordinary Bell test that quantum theory breaks with noise to spare?
known: The claim that one friend allows nothing beyond Bell tests was stated for two settings only.
A 2024 list of the exceptions seems not to cover one friend with three settings; no such test is published.
directions.cheapest_test: On a laptop, list every boundary of the one-friend, three-setting case, then compute how far quantum theory exceeds each and how much noise it survives; chip only if found.
directions.human_prompt: Is a laptop search for a new, stronger version of the Wigner's-friend test (a puzzle about whether what one observer sees is a fact for everyone), the kind that would make next month's chip test about half as expensive, worth a few hours of laptop time (free)? Will it come back a hit? This one is decided by mathematics, not by the chip, and is scored on its own line.

directions.title: Maximally ψ-epistemic models in d = 4, with no fair sampling
directions.odds_event: S + 5σ < 1 under both choices of ωq (intended states and tomography-reconstructed states), on raw counts with no post-selection.
directions.question: Can the chip rule out theories where quantum states overlap only because of our ignorance, counting every result and discarding none?
known: A photon experiment ruled these theories out (score 0.690), but only by assuming lost photons were typical.
A related test (PBR) passed on this chip type, but its threshold came from the authors' own noise model.
directions.cheapest_test: Use two qubits as one four-level system, prepare 5 states and test 10 pairs (30 circuits x 2,000 shots), plus state checks, scoring raw counts with nothing discarded.
directions.human_prompt: Is testing whether a quantum state is something real or only a summary of our ignorance, counting every result with none thrown away, worth about 21 seconds of chip time? Will it come back a hit?
engine_only: the exact threshold in the pass rule

directions.prior_work_line: Ringbauer et al. 2015 (arXiv:1412.6213, photons, d=4) found S 0.690(1) assuming fair sampling and say that without it detection efficiency must exceed 0.976 (d=4, n=5), an error budget of a few per cent. Yang, Yuan and Barnes 2025 (arXiv:2510.11213, ibm_marrakesh Heron r2) measured 0.2-0.6% forbidden-outcome rates on adjacent pairs in a PBR test. Together these predict S below 1 by a thin margin. No superconducting d≥3 test exists (two searches).

directions.title: Can extra readout error stand in for P3-5c's blur term?
directions.assumption_at_stake: The blur-type term P3-5c needed is error in the chip's state, not readout error beyond the job's own calibration.
directions.cheapest_test: Refit P3-5c's models on the archive with four readout knobs per pair, bounded at 3x the binomial error of the job's own calibration; parametric bootstrap as P3-5c. Design files already being prepared by another session (experiments/p3_17_readout.py, uncommitted at remap time).
directions.models: none: archived chip data, no model (rule 12 does not apply)
directions.odds_event: With readout knobs bounded at 3x each job's calibration error, the blur-type term is still needed (p < 0.01) on all three archived pairs. (Remap draft; if P3-17's pre-registration states a different event, it logs the change and both odds stay.)
directions.odds_rationale: The ng-p3-5c audit found readout can absorb blur on h221 and h268 only with knobs of 2.7-5% per qubit, 3-20 times IBM's reported error; 3x the calibration's own binomial error is far tighter. Risk: h088 already misfits, and tight bounds may still help on the weakest pair. Above the running base rate 8/19 = 0.42 (ledger/brier.md); program 3 is 0 hits in 4 scored.

directions.prior_work_line: Readout drift on IBM qubits is reported as small and stepwise: Hirasaki et al. 2023 (arXiv:2307.04337) saw error-rate steps lasting minutes at about 1% assignment error, and Pal et al. 2026 (arXiv:2601.08290) found drift surviving full readout mitigation, so in preparation, not readout. directions.cheapest_test: One new job: program 1's three witness circuits on their original qubits, 9 tomography settings x 2,000 shots each, plus readout calibration; P3-5c's fits, unchanged.
